human.title: Venezuela: the largest Chinese lending in the region, and no trade to measure it against
human.author: AI-drafted from the site's indicators; not yet reviewed by the project owner
human.text_md:
## Alignment

Venezuela has no index: it reports no mineral trade to UN Comtrade in the covered years, so every trade-based component is absent and fewer than three components remain [index_component:VEN]. What the site holds is money: US$22.5 bn of documented Chinese commitments over 2015–2021, the largest of any of the twelve, after peaks of US$21.0 bn in 2010 and US$14.4 bn in 2013, nine of them flagged as large relative to GDP; no US commitment is recorded [flow_finance:CN:VEN:2015-2021] [flow_finance:CN:VEN:2010] [anomaly_flag:large_commitment]. No statement, legislative record or headline is coded [coverage:VEN]. My reading: Venezuela is the clearest case of influence bought with loans that the mineral trade record cannot see, and the site is right to show it as an absence rather than a number.

## Trajectory

None can be measured from trade. The loan years are 2010–2015; nothing documented after 2021, because the Chinese source ends there [flow_finance:CN:VEN:2015-2021].

## Risks and likely next moves

No forecast is published [forecast:VEN]. In my reading the question for 2026 is whether the political change of January 2026 and the mining talks reported in the press produce reported trade or documented US commitments; either would appear on the site before any interpretation could.

## What would change this reading

Reported mineral trade; a US commitment in the DFC or EXIM record; or statements by Venezuelan officials in the dataset.
